question: What fixed points and phase transitions arise when normalized token representations repeatedly generate their own self-attention graph, particularly when token count and representation dimension grow together?

key_findings.claim: A nonvanishing within-cluster overlap advantage makes a broad family of exactly aligned token partitions fixed points in the ordered high-dimensional limit.
key_findings.evidence: For a token in cluster a, total relative leakage is bounded by (N-n_a)/(n_a-1) times exp[-beta sqrt(d) Delta_a]. If beta sqrt(d) Delta_a minus the cluster-count entropy diverges, attention remains inside the source cluster and every center is unchanged by the normalized residual update. At d=N, any fixed positive gap suffices for fixed beta>0.

key_findings.claim: Attention condensation and representation diversity are independent axes of a clustered attractor.
key_findings.evidence: The mean attention IPR depends on cluster sizes: O(1) macroscopic clusters yield Y_A=O(1/N), whereas bounded microscopic clusters yield Y_A=O(1). The Gram participation rank also depends on center geometry: extensively many random microscopic centers give R_eff=Theta(N), while the same number confined to a common cone can have R_eff=O(1).

key_findings.claim: The clustered manifold is normally attracting but has neutral collective directions, so infinitesimal width heals while cluster centers remain free to move along the limiting manifold.
key_findings.evidence: Writing perturbations as a cluster mean rotation plus zero-mean internal deviations, the residual update leaves the collective mode unchanged and multiplies each internal mode by 1-gamma n_a/(n_a-1). Thus 0<gamma<1 contracts every cluster size n_a>=2 when leakage vanishes; finite leakage instead causes exponentially slow center drift.

key_findings.claim: A finite random width can fragment a macroscopic parent cluster, with beta times width squared as the effective sharpness.
key_findings.evidence: For perturbation amplitude epsilon, the common overlap cancels from every softmax row and the centered logit variance is epsilon^4, leaving alpha=beta epsilon^2 as the control. Simulations at N=4096 and T=N for five epsilon values collapse when plotted against alpha: the largest-cluster fraction falls while the attention IPR becomes finite. This is a finite-amplitude basin transition, not a linear instability of the exactly aligned state.

key_findings.claim: Extensive microscopic fragmentation is stable at any fixed positive sharpness only when the thermodynamic limit precedes the long-time limit.
key_findings.evidence: For random bounded-size clusters at d=N, the maximum cross-center overlap is o(1), so leakage scales like exp[-beta sqrt(N)+O(sqrt(log N))+log N]. The predicted coarsening lifetime is approximately exp(beta sqrt(N) Delta)/(gamma N), and random-pair simulations collapse log(N tau_pair) against beta sqrt(N) Delta with the predicted unit slope. Every finite system can still coarsen if time is taken to infinity first.

anchors.section: Stability of extensive fragmentation and Figure 2

key_findings.claim: An initially unstructured Gaussian cloud undergoes a finite-sharpness dynamical condensation and accesses three distinct finite-time regimes.
key_findings.evidence: At small beta, diffuse averaging produces rank collapse. At intermediate beta, finite attention IPR and a peak in row-centered overlap variance accompany coexistence of one macroscopic cluster with extensive microscopic clusters. At larger beta, the macroscopic cluster disappears while attention remains condensed and normalized participation rank becomes finite, indicating broadly separated microscopic fragments. Results over N=512-4096 at T=N show an onset that does not drift to the static random-energy threshold beta proportional to sqrt(log N).

anchors.section: Dynamical accessibility from Gaussian initial conditions

key_findings.claim: Softmax's nonlinear amplification is essential to fixed-beta microscopic condensation in this scaling regime, but an exponential kernel is not uniquely required.
key_findings.evidence: A static Gaussian row remains diffuse at fixed beta and localizes only around beta proportional to sqrt(log M). A dynamically created O(1) overlap gap instead gives an O(sqrt(N)) logit advantage. Affine attention still has IPR O(1/N), while a positive polynomial kernel [u]_+^p reaches O(1) IPR at the threshold p=2 and fully dominates for p>2.

key_findings.claim: Macroscopic coherence grows by amplifying an O(N^{-1/2}) finite-sample polarization, producing logarithmic formation time distinct from microscopic nucleation and eventual coarsening.
key_findings.evidence: Under uniform attention, a permutation-symmetric mean-field closure gives s_t=[1+(N-1)(1-eta_N)^{2t}]^{-1} and t_s=log(N-1)/[-2 log|1-eta_N|]. Simulations at beta=0 and 0.4 follow this logistic collapse; at beta=0.8 broad polarization precedes the later formation of a 0.99-overlap macroscopic cluster. The proposed hierarchy is t_micro=O(1), t_macro=O(log N), and t_coarsen much larger than log N.

method.core_idea: Model depth as repeated normalized residual self-attention on N fixed-norm particles and characterize its attractors through the gap between within-cluster and nearest cross-cluster overlaps.
method.mechanism: Each token has norm sqrt(d), self-edges are masked, logits are sqrt(d) times normalized dot products, and a softmax with inverse temperature beta defines the interaction graph. The normalized residual update with gamma=0.3 feeds that graph back into token geometry. Exact aligned partitions yield closed-form coarse cluster attention and leakage bounds. Tangent perturbation analysis separates neutral center rotations from contracting internal widths. Random-energy calculations provide a frozen-logit control; two-level rows compare softmax, affine, and polynomial kernels. Simulations from aligned-plus-noise, random pairs, Gaussian clouds, and nearly rank-collapsed cones use attention IPR/entropy, overlap variance, Gram participation rank, largest-cluster fraction, and cluster count to resolve the phases.
assumptions: Token dimension and token count grow together, usually d=N; the fixed-d, N-to-infinity limit has different condensation behavior.
The repeated layer uses tied identity query, key, and value geometry with masked self-attention, spherical normalization, and a fixed residual coefficient.
Cluster states are exactly internally aligned and contain at least two tokens because diagonal self-attention is excluded.
Claims of thermodynamic stability assume a positive overlap advantage and take N to infinity before the long-time limit.
Random center concentration and tangent-noise isotropy are representative of the broad and narrow-cone fragmented states analyzed.
Finite-time phase diagrams measured at T=N or a few multiples of N represent long-lived plateaus, not exact stationary states at finite N.

techniques.role: Balances the exponential softmax advantage of an aligned cluster against the entropy of all external targets.
Aggregates token-level attention into a row-stochastic matrix over cluster centers with exact size multiplicities.
Separates neutral collective cluster rotations from zero-mean internal deformations that the residual update contracts.
Derives the localization threshold for frozen Gaussian logits to distinguish static extreme-value selection from feedback-driven condensation.
Tests how affine, polynomial, and exponential attention convert an O(sqrt(N)) generated logit gap into row localization.
Combines attention IPR and entropy, overlap variance, participation rank, largest-cluster size, and cluster count because no single statistic distinguishes all regimes.
Rescales pair-cluster merger times by beta sqrt(N) times the gap to test the exponentially long metastability prediction.
Reduces uniform-attention consensus formation to amplification of the sample's initial O(N^{-1/2}) mean direction.

evaluations.setting: Single macroscopic cluster with five imposed noise amplitudes, N=d=4096, observation time T=N
evaluations.metric: Largest-cluster fraction and mean attention IPR versus alpha=beta epsilon^2
evaluations.result: Curves collapse across epsilon, with fragmentation coinciding with loss of the macroscopic cluster and onset of finite attention localization.
evaluations.baseline: The same curves plotted against raw beta or epsilon separately

evaluations.setting: N/2 initially aligned random pairs for N=512, 1024, and 2048
evaluations.metric: Time until all pair centers reach overlap 1-1e-4
evaluations.result: log(N tau_pair) collapses against beta sqrt(N) Delta with the predicted unit slope.

evaluations.setting: Normalized Gaussian initial states, N=d from 512 to 4096, T=N
evaluations.metric: Attention IPR/entropy, overlap variance, participation rank, largest cluster, and number of clusters
evaluations.result: The joint diagnostics resolve diffuse rank collapse, macroscopic-cluster/fragment coexistence, and broad microscopic fragmentation as beta increases.
evaluations.baseline: Frozen Gaussian-logit REM, whose fixed-beta IPR vanishes

evaluations.setting: Gaussian states at N=2048 observed at T=N,2N,3N,4N,5N
evaluations.metric: Time sensitivity of all six phase observables
evaluations.result: Curves nearly coincide, indicating a long-lived plateau by T=N over the measured window.

evaluations.setting: Nearly rank-collapsed initial states with epsilon=0.1, N=512-4096
evaluations.metric: The same attention and cluster statistics plus unnormalized overlap variance and participation rank
evaluations.result: Alpha controls fragmentation, but V and R_eff remain O(1), showing that extensive microscopic clusters can remain in one low-rank cone.
evaluations.baseline: Gaussian initial states, whose broad fragmentation has R_eff=Theta(N)

evaluations.setting: Uniform and weakly heterogeneous attention from Gaussian initialization
evaluations.metric: Time for polarization s to reach 1/2 and time for a 0.99-overlap cluster to contain half the tokens
evaluations.result: At beta=0 and 0.4 polarization follows the logistic O(log N) law; at beta=0.8 polarization becomes macroscopic before tight cluster sharpening.

evaluations.setting: Cluster extraction at N=4096 under thresholds 1-q_th in {1e-3,1e-4,1e-5}
evaluations.metric: Largest-cluster size and total cluster count
evaluations.result: The 1e-4 and 1e-5 choices nearly coincide, while 1e-3 merges nearby fragments; subsequent results use q_th=1-1e-4.

limitations: Author-stated: the theory focuses on d proportional to N; fixed dimension cannot sustain the same fixed-beta microscopic attention condensation.
Author-stated: nontrivial query, key, and value maps, multihead interaction, MLP sublayers, training, and architecture-specific normalization are left for future work.
Author-stated: finite-N fragmented states retain nonzero leakage and can coarsen; stability depends on taking N to infinity before time to infinity.
Author-stated: finite-time diagrams at T=N do not prove exact stationarity, and narrow-cone states continue evolving visibly through 5N.
Reviewer-identified: existence of a finite-beta condensation onset from a Gaussian cloud is established numerically, not by an analytic critical beta or a rigorous nucleation theorem.
Reviewer-identified: the stability argument is conditional on a surviving O(1) overlap gap; it does not prove that generic dynamics create that gap with high probability.

Reviewer-identified: tied, identity-map, self-masked dynamics are a severe abstraction from trained transformers, so links to attention sinks, semantic clusters, or model quality are hypotheses rather than validated consequences.
Reviewer-identified: clustering uses a hand-set near-unity connectivity threshold and the transition is diagnosed from a finite set of system sizes and random realizations.
Reviewer-identified: no downstream task, learned attention map, or real model activation is evaluated, leaving the operational meaning of the phases untested.
failure_modes: If dimension grows more slowly than needed for sqrt(d) gaps to beat log N target entropy, microscopic rows remain diffuse at fixed beta.
A cluster with a gap shrinking faster than (log N)/sqrt(N) leaks enough attention to merge or lose its fixed-point character.
Taking long time before large N selects consensus even when the ordered thermodynamic limit retains extensive fragments.
Small perturbations contract, but finite perturbations can cross the basin boundary and split a macroscopic cluster into many descendants.
An affine or too-low-degree attention kernel cannot turn the generated gap into O(1) IPR, despite adaptive geometry.
A single attention-localization statistic conflates broad high-rank fragmentation with narrow-cone low-rank fragmentation.
Finite cluster thresholds can merge nearby descendants and misstate both largest-cluster size and cluster count.
More realistic learned Q/K/V maps may rotate, shear, or destabilize the overlap structure on which the identity-map gap argument relies.
reusable_insights: Compare the energetic advantage of a preferred interaction to the logarithm of the number of competitors; local similarity alone is not enough to establish routing concentration.
Separate whether attention is sparse from whether representations are geometrically diverse; use both a row-concentration statistic and a Gram-spectrum statistic.
State the order of thermodynamic and long-time limits explicitly whenever metastability is promoted to stability.
A scale collapse such as alpha=beta epsilon^2 can reveal the effective control variable of a finite-amplitude transition.
Use a frozen-random-logit control to show when a phase is generated by feedback rather than ordinary extreme-value softmax behavior.
Distinguish local normal attraction, finite-amplitude basin escape, and inter-attractor coarsening; they occur on different perturbation and time scales.
Multiple complementary observables are necessary when local interaction topology and global representation geometry can decouple.
An O(N^{-1/2}) sample asymmetry can become macroscopic in O(log N) repeated layers under multiplicative feedback.
open_questions: Can one prove a finite critical beta and the high-probability nucleation of overlap gaps from Gaussian initial conditions?
Which parts of the attractor manifold survive learned, anisotropic Q/K/V maps, multiple heads, MLP sublayers, residual scaling, and standard layer normalization?
Do analogous attention-condensation diagnostics predict training stability, retrieval, in-context learning, or representation quality in real transformers?
What phase diagram results when d and N grow at a general ratio or different rates rather than exactly d=N?
Can finite-size coarsening be reduced to an effective stochastic dynamics over cluster sizes and center overlaps?
How do causal masks and positional encodings alter the overlap-gap condition and the extensive fragmented manifold?
Can learning tune beta or the attention kernel across the polynomial threshold and thereby control fragmentation intentionally?
Is the intermediate macroscopic-cluster coexistence regime a true asymptotic phase or a long crossover at the available sizes and times?

competitive_landscape.title: The emergence of clusters in self-attention dynamics
competitive_landscape.difference: Geshkovski et al. introduce the interacting-particle view and prove long-time clustering whose limiting objects depend on value-matrix spectrum. This paper specializes to normalized identity-map dynamics in d proportional to N and adds an overlap-gap fixed-manifold analysis, attention condensation, extensive microscopic fragmentation, and a finite-sharpness nucleation diagram.

competitive_landscape.title: Dynamic metastability in the self-attention model
competitive_landscape.difference: Dynamic Metastability rigorously proves exponentially long multicluster trapping followed by eventual single-cluster collapse in a spherical self-attention gradient flow. The present work derives a different high-dimensional overlap-gap lifetime exp(beta sqrt(N) Delta) and emphasizes order-of-limits stability plus extensive bounded-size fragmentation.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergence of meta-stable clustering in mean-field transformer models
competitive_landscape.difference: Bruno et al. perturb a continuous-time mean-field PDE around uniform initialization and identify metastable structures through Gegenbauer modes as a function of inverse temperature. This paper instead studies finite particles with d proportional to N, a discrete normalized residual update, microscopic attention IPR, and overlap-gap-protected attractors.

competitive_landscape.title: Analysis of mean-field models arising from self-attention dynamics in transformer architectures with layer normalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Burger et al. develop a Wasserstein-gradient-flow framework on the sphere and analyze stationary measures and interaction-energy extrema. The current paper uses explicit finite-N cluster partitions and thermodynamic logit-gap scaling to separate attention localization from representation rank.

competitive_landscape.title: Clustering in Causal Attention Masking
competitive_landscape.difference: Karagodin et al. extend clustering theory to causally masked attention and arbitrary key-query matrices with identity value map, proving single-cluster convergence and partial metastability results. The present model is bidirectional/self-masked and less architecturally general, but gives a sharper high-dimensional condensation and fragmented-manifold picture.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: a finite overlap gap is the organizing quantity for a high-dimensional manifold of clustered fixed points, its perturbative stability, and a feedback-driven attention-condensation transition accessible from Gaussian tokens. Reviewer inference after comparison: clustering and exponentially long metastability in self-attention were already established, including mean-field phase formation and causal-mask variants. The defensible novelty is the joint d~N microscopic-condensation regime, the explicit leakage-versus-entropy criterion, the separation of attention IPR from representation rank, and the three-regime finite-time diagram. The generic dynamical transition remains less secure than the conditional attractor analysis because its critical point and nucleation are numerical rather than rigorously derived, and realism beyond the identity-map toy dynamics is unvalidated.
reviewer_notes: Read all 31 extracted pages, including the random-energy control, kernel-scaling calculation, complete cluster stability analysis, logistic formation theory, and all finite-size/time diagnostics. Page anchors use PDF pages, so supplemental section numbering begins on page 7. Primary competitors were checked on arXiv/OpenReview. Claims about generic nucleation, asymptotic phase status, and transformer relevance are explicitly reviewer inference.
